subject: Chemistry
description: Acidic, basic, amphoteric oxides; rust; corrosion; oxidation states

questions.stem: RUST formed on iron is chemically:
questions.explanation: RUST — hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. Formed when iron is exposed to BOTH water (or moisture) AND oxygen — neither alone is enough. Reddish-brown, flaky. Doesn't protect underlying metal (unlike aluminium oxide which forms a dense protective layer). Prevention: galvanising (zinc coating), painting, oiling, alloying (stainless steel — adds Cr, Ni). Distractors 1, 3, 4 are different iron compounds.

questions.stem: AMPHOTERIC OXIDES are those that react with both acids and bases. An example is:

options.option_text: Sodium oxide (Na₂O), only basic in water
Aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃), reacts with acids and bases

questions.explanation: AMPHOTERIC = reacts with both acids and bases. Examples: Al₂O₃, ZnO, BeO, SnO, PbO. Al₂O₃ + HCl → AlCl₃ + H₂O (acts basic). Al₂O₃ + NaOH → NaAlO₂ (sodium aluminate, acts acidic). BASIC oxides = metal oxides (Na₂O, CaO, MgO) — react with acids; form bases in water. ACIDIC oxides = non-metal oxides (CO₂, SO₃, NO₂) — react with bases; form acids in water (CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ carbonic acid).

options.option_text: Loss of oxygen by a substance only
Loss of electrons by a substance
Gain of hydrogen by a substance
Decrease in temperature of a system

questions.explanation: Modern definition (electron-transfer): OXIDATION = LOSS of electrons. REDUCTION = GAIN of electrons. Mnemonic: OIL RIG (Oxidation Is Loss; Reduction Is Gain). Older oxygen-hydrogen definitions: oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen; reduction = opposite. The electron-transfer definition is broader and includes reactions without oxygen (e.g., Mg + Cl₂ → MgCl₂; Mg loses electrons → oxidised; Cl gains → reduced). REDOX reaction = paired oxidation + reduction.

questions.stem: When iron reacts with chlorine to form ferric chloride (FeCl₃), the OXIDATION STATE of iron changes from:
questions.explanation: Fe (elemental, oxidation state 0) → FeCl₃ (Fe is +3, Cl is −1 each). So Fe lost 3 electrons → oxidised from 0 to +3. Equation: 2Fe + 3Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃. Iron has two common oxidation states: +2 (ferrous, FeCl₂) and +3 (ferric, FeCl₃). With excess Cl₂, FeCl₃ forms preferentially. Distractor 1 = +2 (FeCl₂, different product). Distractor 3, 4 are between non-zero states.

questions.stem: GALVANISATION involves coating iron with which metal to prevent rust?

options.option_text: Zinc, a more reactive sacrificial metal
Tin, used inside food cans for protection
Aluminium, a light silvery metal commonly

questions.explanation: GALVANISATION = coating iron with ZINC. Zinc is MORE REACTIVE than iron → preferentially oxidises (sacrifices itself) → protects iron underneath, even if scratched. Used for fences, roofing sheets, water-supply pipes, car bodies. Methods: hot-dip galvanising, electrogalvanising. TINNING — coating with TIN (used inside food cans; tin is LESS reactive, gives barrier protection only — fails if scratched). Galvanising is more robust. Distractor 1 — copper; not used for iron protection. Distractor 4 — Al used as alloy (aluminised steel for some applications).

questions.stem: Which of these gases is responsible for ACID RAIN?

options.option_text: SO₂ and NOₓ from fossil-fuel combustion
CO₂ and CH₄ greenhouse gases mainly

questions.explanation: Acid Rain — caused mainly by SO₂ (sulphur dioxide) + NOₓ (nitrogen oxides) released from fossil fuels (coal-fired power plants, vehicle exhaust). React with atmospheric water to form sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) and nitric acid (HNO₃). pH < 5.6 (normal rain ~5.6 due to CO₂). Damages forests (Black Forest, Germany), lakes (kills fish), buildings + monuments (Taj Mahal — discoloured by SO₂ from Mathura refinery, prompting court orders), human health (respiratory). Mitigated by FGD (flue-gas desulphurisation) scrubbers, EU Directive cuts. Distractor 3 — greenhouse warming, separate issue. Distractor 4 — ozone depletion, also separate.

questions.stem: When carbon dioxide is dissolved in water, the resulting solution is mildly:

options.option_text: Acidic, due to formation of carbonic acid

questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid, weak). H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻. Result: mildly acidic, pH ~5.6 (compared to neutral 7). This is why rainwater is naturally slightly acidic (NOT acid rain — that's pH < 5.6). Same chemistry: ocean acidification (rising CO₂ → ocean pH dropping ~0.1 since pre-industrial → coral bleaching, shellfish stress). Soda-water + soft drinks rely on CO₂ dissolved → pleasant fizz + tang.
